messages:
maria: Heads up — since ~08:12 UTC we're seeing a cluster-wide uptick in internal DNS timeouts affecting model-serving pods (high tail latency + 502s). Rolling alerts from redis-proxy -> model-router chain.

jason: I see it too, 08:11-08:18 window. coredns logs show a bunch of SERVFAILs and 'message too long' on UDP in front of some nodes.

priya: Interesting — we've been shifting some GPU nodes back onto the RDMA overlay for Dedicated pools. Could be MTU/fragmentation.

alex: Can you paste a sample coredns log and a node-local-dns (nodelocaldns) log? Also which AZ/region?

maria: us-west-2a and 2b. Here's a snippet from a coredns master: 
```
[08:13:14] WARN: plugin/errors: 2 ns IN A: read udp 10.0.0.5:5353->10.0.4.2:53: message too long
[08:13:14] ERROR: plugin/forward: failed to forward: upstream unreachable: dial udp 10.0.4.10:53: i/o timeout
```
And node-local-dns on one of the gpu nodes shows: 
```
E0814 08:13:15.123 1 resolver.go:210] lookup failed: dial udp 127.0.0.53:53: write udp 127.0.0.53:55874->127.0.0.53:53: write: message too long
```

jason: 'message too long' usually indicates EDNS0/UDP size + fragmentation. Did we recently change MTU or enable jumbo frames on the RDMA NICs?

siva: We did a partial MTU tweak last week for RoCE tuning — moved RDMA MTU from 1500 to 9000 on the fabric for the new racks. That was gated to the RDMA VLAN but maybe some overlay paths still hit it.

priya: That could explain asymmetric path handling: packets fragmented on some switches but not others -> upstream DNS replies with EDNS > 1500 get dropped. CoreDNS sometimes falls back to TCP but our node-local DNS proxy tries UDP-only for speed.

alex: Quick repro: from an affected pod run dig +short @10.0.4.10 example.com +dnssec +bufsize=4096. If UDP fails and TCP succeeds, that points at EDNS/frag.

maria: Ran that from model-router-7: 
```
$ dig @10.0.4.10 example.com +bufsize=4096 +time=2
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 12345
;; WARNING: recursion requested but not available
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```
But `dig +tcp @10.0.4.10 example.com` returns answer.

jason: OK that's pretty conclusive. We have UDP path issues (likely fragmentation) and TCP fallback is working but slower — causing timeouts in the 50-200ms budgets for internal RPCs.

priya: Mitigations we can try: 1) reduce EDNS buffer advertised by CoreDNS to 1232, 2) pin node-local-dns to prefer TCP fallback sooner, or 3) enforce uniform MTU across overlays. Which is fastest?

siva: Fastest short-term: reduce EDNS buffer and add iptables rule to force DNS TCP for large responses? We can also push a nodelocaldns config to set upstream bufsize=1232. Long-term we need to audit MTU on the RDMA overlay and ensure PMTU discovery works across VXLAN/Geneve + RoCE.

alex: Also worth checking if we have recent kernel sysctl changes: net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc and net.ipv6.conf.*.disable_ipv6 adjustments can break PMTU.

maria: I can push a CoreDNS ConfigMap change to set 'max_udp_payload_size 1232' in the forward plugin and roll. Want me to do that as a quick experiment?

jason: +1 do it in canary: edit coredns in kube-system in us-west-2a only. Watch 1-minute DNS errors metric and model-router 95p latency.

priya: I'll prepare a nodelocaldns helm patch to set prefer_tcp_on_error: true (not an actual flag, but update the upstream resolver bufsize and retry logic). Keep it minimal.

infra-bot: deploy plan ready: coredns-configmap patch -> patch 'max_udp_payload_size: 1232' -> rolling update(coredns) in kube-system/us-west-2a. Preview OK.

maria: Rolling now on a single master: `kubectl apply -f coredns-payload-1232.yaml --context prod-west-2a`

jason: Watch the graphs: dns.query.errors and dns.latency tail. If TCP fallback keeps handling the rest, we should see errors drop within 60-120s.

(5 min pass)

maria: After the change, dns SERVFAILs in 2a dropped ~80%, model-router 95p latency dropped from 210ms to 75ms. Very promising.

siva: Good. That shows fragmentation/EDNS is the main culprit. Still need the full fix: validate MTU on all hops, ensure VXLAN/Geneve overhead accounted for, and confirm RoCE path doesn't cause silent drops for fragmented packets.

alex: Action items: 
- siva: run end-to-end MTU/fragmentation trace across RDMA VLAN, VXLAN overlay and TORs (test pmtud + sendpath).
- priya: prepare small nodelocaldns release that lowers upstream bufsize and enables quicker TCP fallback.
- maria: revert canary to all masters after merge if green; then roll to 2b.
- jason: add alert rule for sudden increase in 'dns udp message too long' and a runbook blurb about EDNS/MTU.

priya: I'll also add a short note in the Dedicated onboarding docs: "If enabling jumbo MTU for RDMA, coordinate with networking to update overlay MTU and test DNS EDNS handling."

maria: Thanks — I'll keep this thread updated. If anyone sees residual 502/timeout, ping here with pod names. :thumbsup:

jason: Nice quick mitigation. We'll follow up on long-term network config audit.

siva: Starting MTU trace now, will post results in channel.

maria: Closing loop for now, moving to postmortem if we see recurrence.
notes: canary patch mitigated issue; root cause likely EDNS+fragmentation across RDMA/jumbo frame boundaries
